sentiment.rationale: The document shows strong operational momentum with record fourth-quarter results, double-digit adjusted EPS growth, and record sales in RIS, but forward guidance is not formally raised; management expresses confidence in the New Frontier strategy and 2026 outlook. The score reflects genuine operational momentum and confident forward language, but is tempered by the absence of a formal guidance raise and some mixed segment results (Asia flat, Latin America down on a reported basis).

summary.revenue: Premiums, fees and other revenues (PFOs) increased 29% to $18.7 billion in Q4 2025; full-year PFOs increased 10% to $57.6 billion. Adjusted PFOs, excluding PRT, were up 8% to $12.8 billion in Q4 and up 5% to $49.8 billion for the full year.
summary.eps: Q4 2025 net income per share was $1.17, down 34% from $1.78 in Q4 2024. Adjusted earnings per share, excluding total notable items, increased 24% to $2.58 in Q4 and 10% to $8.89 for the full year.
summary.guidance: The document does not provide explicit forward guidance for 2026, but management expresses confidence in the New Frontier strategy and states the foundation built in 2025 positions MetLife to 'accelerate growth responsibly and deploy capital prudently.'
summary.margin: Direct expense ratio, excluding total notable items related to direct expenses and PRT, was 11.6% in Q4 2025 and 11.7% for the full year, compared to 13.1% in Q4 2024 and 12.1% for full year 2024. Adjusted ROE, excluding total notable items, was 18.3% in Q4 and 16.0% for the full year.
key_risks: Net derivative losses of $646 million in Q4 due to higher long-term interest rates, stronger equity markets, and strengthening of the U.S. dollar.
Net investment losses of $160 million in Q4 reflecting normal trading activity.
Japan macroeconomic volatility (FX and rates) causing temporary fluctuations in sales and slightly higher surrender activity in Q4.
Group disability pressure in Q4 with slightly higher average severity and lower Social Security decisions.
Potential impact of AI-driven employment actions on group benefits business, though incorporated into outlook.
Structural risks from forward-looking statements including interest rates, credit spreads, equity markets, and global economic conditions.
key_opportunities: Record RIS sales including $14.2 billion in PRT and $11.1 billion of U.K. longevity reinsurance.
US retail retirement space entry via flow reinsurance deals with two partners.
PineBridge acquisition closed December 30, 2025, expanding MIM to $742B total AUM.
Strong sales growth in Asia (up 18% constant currency), Latin America (up 26% constant currency), and EMEA (up 24% constant currency).
Group Benefits disability and paid family medical leave as growth opportunities with bundled sales.
Higher interest rates increasing attractiveness of fixed rate products.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: CEO Michel Khalaf states 'We are confident that the foundation built in 2025 positions MetLife to accelerate growth responsibly and deploy capital prudently to deliver on our New Frontier commitments.'
